utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-08-91-A, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Before starting, can -- before starting, can I make sure -- I would like to make sure that all parties hear the proceedings in a language that they understand. Mr. Stanisic -- oh, you had no translation. I'm sorry. Interpreter, could you repeat the question to -- and if not, I will repeat it. Yes, I can. I will repeat the question. Mr. Stanisic, can you -- are you able to follow the proceedings in a language you understand? Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STANISIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, yes, and I can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Stanisic. As we know, in any event I will note it for the record, Mr. Zupljanin waived his right to attend this Status Conference. I will now ask for the appearances of the parties. Since we already have gone through the two principal parties, Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Zupljanin, I will turn to the representatives -- their representatives for the Defence of Mr. Stanisic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Slobodan Zecevic and Stefan Bourgon appearing for Stanisic Defence this afternoon. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. It's nice to see Mr. Bourgon again. The Defence for Mr. Zupljanin, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Tatjana Cmeric appearing today on behalf of Mr. Zupljanin. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Cmeric. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BASSETT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Marisa Bassett for the Prosecution with my colleague, senior appeals counsel, Helen Brady; and our case manager, Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Bassett. This Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present case, parties filed their Notices of Appeal on 13 May 2013 and the first Status Conference was held on 4 September 2013. Today's Status Conference is the second in this case and was scheduled by an order issued on 2 December 2013. I turn to detention conditions and health of Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Zupljanin. First I would like to inquire into the status of the detention conditions and health conditions. If you have any concerns, Mr. Stanisic and the counsel for Mr. Zupljanin, in relation to the detention conditions or your state of health, I would invite you to raise them now. If you wish, this discussion can take place in private session. Is there any request for a private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There is no request for private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I see that both -- neither Mr. Stanisic nor the counsel for Mr. Zupljanin is --

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- is requesting a private session, so we will continue in an open session. Let me turn to recent procedural history since the last Status Conference. With regard to the briefing of the case, on 8 October 2013, the Appeals Chamber granted Mr. Zupljanin's request for leave to amend his Notice of Appeal dated 12 August 2013. Mr. Zupljanin filed the amended version of his Notice of Appeal on 9 October 2013, in which he included an additional ground of appeal and an additional subground of appeal. Mr. Zupljanin had already included his arguments on these grounds in his appeal brief dated 19 August 2013. All parties filed their response briefs on 21 October 2013. The Prosecution's response included arguments on Mr. Zupljanin's additional grounds. All parties filed their reply briefs on 11 November 2013. I will now continue with an overview of the pending motions and the decisions rendered in this case. On 2 July 2013, Mr. Stanisic filed two motions: One motion seeking admission of additional evidence pursuant to Rule 115 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and one motion seeking leave to amend his Notice of Appeal. On 23 July 2013, I assigned Judge Agius to consider both motions. On 24 July 2013, Judge Agius assigned Judge Sekule to replace me on the Bench for the purpose of considering these two motions. On 9 September 2013, Mr. Zupljanin filed a second request to amend his Notice of Appeal and to supplement his appeal brief. On 10 September 2013, I assigned Judge Agius to consider the motion. On 28 November 2013, Judge Agius assigned Judge Sekule to replace me on the Bench for the purpose of considering this motion. On 21 October 2013, Mr. Zupljanin filed a motion to vacate the trial judgement as well as a motion requesting the recusal of Judge Liu from deciding on this motion. On 22 October 2013, I referred both motions to Judge Agius for appropriate action. On 28 November 2013, Judge Agius assigned Judge Sekule to replace me on the Bench for the purpose of considering these motions. On 3 December 2013, Judge Agius, as acting President, rendered the decision denying the request for recusal of Judge Liu, treating it as a motion for disqualification. On 22 October 2013, Mr. Zupljanin filed a request for provisional release pending resolution of his motion to vacate the trial judgement. On 23 October 2013, I referred the motion to Judge Agius for appropriate action. On 28 November 2013, Judge Agius assigned Judge Sekule to replace me on the Bench for the purpose of considering this motion. On 23 October 2013, Mr. Stanisic filed two motions, one motion requesting a declaration of mistrial and another motion requesting provisional release until adjudication of the first motion. On 25 October 2013, I referred both motions to Judge Agius for appropriate action. On 28 November 2013, Judge Agius assigned Judge Sekule to replace me on the Bench for the purpose of considering these two motions. With regard to the provisional release motions, Judge Agius has informed me that these decisions will be issued this week or early next week. As for the other motions pending in this case that were mentioned earlier, Judge Agius has informed me that they will be addressed either before the judicial recess or shortly thereafter. In addition, there are two motions pending in this case presided over by me on which I will now render oral decisions. First, on 3 December 2013, Mr. Zupljanin filed an application in which he seeks leave to substitute the English translation of Exhibit 2D00132 with a revised translation that he recently obtained through the Conference and Languages Services Section. Mr. Zupljanin argues that the existing translation omits a word that is clearly visible in the B/C/S original. Mr. Zupljanin adds that the translation was submitted for revision and has been circulated to the parties. On 4 December 2013, the Prosecution responded that it does not oppose the application. I note that Exhibit 2D00132 was admitted by the Trial Chamber on 20 January 2011. Therefore, pursuant to Rules 54 and 107 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, I, as pre-Appeal Judge, grant the application and instruct the Registrar of the Tribunal to upload the revised version of the English translation. Second, a motion was filed on 9 December 2013 by Mr. Radovan Karadzic, seeking access to the B/C/S audio recordings of the testimony of Witness ST-245 in this case. Mr. Zupljanin responded on the same day and does not oppose the motion. The Prosecution responded on 10 December 2013 and also does not oppose the motion. I note that Mr. Stanisic has not yet responded and I give him the opportunity to do so now. Mr. Stanisic or his counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Your Honour, we intended to file a motion today, but since this is the opportunity, we are sitting in a Status Conference, and Your Honour already said that it will be the oral ruling, I can make my submissions now, with the leave of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do not oppose the motion by Karadzic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since there is no objection from the representative of Mr. Stanisic, I note -- we will proceed. I note that on 30 June 2010, the Trial Chamber ordered the disclosure on an ongoing basis to Radovan Karadzic of all closed and private session testimony transcripts not subject to Rule 70. As part of the disclosure, Mr. Karadzic was granted access to the transcript of the testimony of Witness ST-245, who testified in the trial proceedings in Stanisic and Zupljanin from 2 to 4 November 2010. In this circumstance, I find that Mr. Karadzic already has access to the content of the testimony of Witness ST-245 in the form of a transcript. Mr. Karadzic's request to be granted access to the B/C/S audio recording of this testimony is consequently one of form and not of substance. I therefore grant the application and order the Registrar of the Tribunal to provide Mr. Karadzic with the B/C/S audio recording of the testimony of Witness ST-245 and to inform Mr. Karadzic and the Karadzic Chamber of this decision. At this point I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise. Counsel for Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We have no other issues at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You have no other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you counsel for Mr. Stanisic. Counsel for Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. CMERIC
utterances.text: No other issues at this stage on behalf of Mr. Zupljanin either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BASSETT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we have no issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, counsel for the Prosecution. I believe that this concludes today's Status Conference. I thank the parties for their attendance. I thank the staff of the Registry and I thank particularly the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.47 p.m.
